subject: Business Models
title: Decentralized Autonomous Organizations
description: A 60-second lesson on Decentralized Autonomous Organizations.

hook.text: A DAO is a company with no CEO, no office, and no employees—just code and token holders who vote on decisions.

buildup.text: DAOs use blockchain smart contracts to automate governance. Token holders vote on spending, strategy, and rules.

discovery.text: ConstitutionDAO raised $47 million in a week from 17,000 strangers to buy a copy of the US Constitution.

twist.text: Most DAOs suffer from voter apathy. Less than 10% of token holders actually vote on proposals.

climax.text: DAOs are an experiment in leaderless organizations. The model is promising but governance challenges remain.

punchline.text: No CEO, no office, token-based votes. DAOs reimagine how organizations run.

quiz.question: What is the main governance challenge DAOs face?
options: Voter apathy with less than 10% participation

details.summary: Decentralized autonomous organizations use blockchain smart contracts to encode governance rules, enabling communities to make collective decisions without traditional management hierarchies. Token holders vote on proposals, and code automatically executes approved decisions.
details.whyItMatters: DAOs experiment with new forms of collective ownership and governance. Though still early, they challenge assumptions about how organizations must be structured and could transform how communities pool resources and make decisions.
takeaways: Smart contracts encode governance rules that execute automatically
Token holders vote on proposals without centralized management
DAOs experiment with collective ownership of protocols and treasuries

faq.question: How does decision-making work in a DAO?
faq.answer: Members submit proposals that other token holders vote on. Voting weight typically corresponds to token holdings. If a proposal passes the required threshold, the smart contract executes it automatically. This removes the need for a board of directors or CEO.

faq.question: What are the main challenges facing DAOs currently?
faq.answer: Low voter participation, plutocratic governance where wealthy holders dominate, legal liability uncertainty, vulnerability to smart contract exploits, difficulty making rapid decisions, and the tension between decentralization ideals and practical need for coordination.
